title: Lavandula dentata

''Lavandula santolinifolia'' }} '''''Lavandula dentata''''', the '''fringed lavender''' or '''French lavender''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Lamiaceae]], [[Native species|native]] to the [[Mediterranean basin]], [[Eritrea]], [[Ethiopia]], [[Yemen]], and the [[Arabian Peninsula]].{{cite web|title=''Lavandula dentata''|publisher=Plants Of the World Online |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:449031-1 | access-date=20 August 2023|date=2023}} Growing to {{convert|60|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall, it has gray-green, linear or lance-shaped leaves with toothed edges and a lightly woolly texture.{{cite book|last=Bayer|first=E. |author2=Buttler |author3=Finkenzeller |author4=Grau |title=Plantas del Mediterráneo|year=1989 |location=Barcelona |publisher=Blume |isbn=84-7031-629-X}} The long-lasting, narrow spikes of purple flowers, topped with pale violet bracts, first appear in late spring. The whole plant is strongly aromatic with the typical lavender fragrance.{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}} Its native [[habitat]] includes low hills with [[limestone]] substrates amidst other shrubs. It is present on Madeira and the [[Canary Islands]].{{cite book|last=López González|first=Ginés A.|title=Guía de los árboles y arbustos de la Península Ibérica y Baleares|year=2007|publisher=Ediciones Mundi-Prensa |editor=Madrid:Mundi-Prensa|isbn= 978-84-8476-312-3}} One of several species known by the English common name French lavender (see also ''[[Lavandula stoechas]]''), it is commonly grown as an [[ornamental plant]] and its [[essential oil]] is used in perfumes.{{Cite web |url=http://ecocrop.fao.org/ecocrop/srv/en/cropView?id=7174 |title=FAO |access-date=2010-07-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100727223348/http://ecocrop.fao.org/ecocrop/srv/en/cropView?id=7174 |archive-date=2010-07-27 |url-status=dead }} Like other lavenders, it is particularly associated with dry, sunny, well-drained conditions in [[Alkali soil|alkaline soil]]. But it will tolerate a range of conditions, though it may be short-lived. The [[cultivar]] ''L. dentata'' var. ''dentata'' 'Royal Crown' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Lavandula dentata'' var. ''dentata'' 'Royal Crown' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/108219/Lavandula-dentata-var-dentata-Royal-Crown/Details | access-date=23 February 2020}}{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 59 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 19 March 2018}} It requires some shelter in frost-prone areas. ==Gallery== Lavanduladentata.jpg|{{Center|Woolly leaf texture}} Starr 070402-6271 Lavandula dentata.jpg|{{Center|Toothed leaves}} Starr 071024-0197 Lavandula dentata.jpg|{{Center|Purple flowers}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons}} * [http://www.plantoftheweek.org/week496.shtml Plant of the Week] {{Taxonbar|from=Q1450735}} [[Category:Lavandula|dentata]] [[Category:Flora of Spain]] [[Category:Garden plants of Europe]] [[Category:Drought-tolerant plants]] [[Category:Medicinal plants]] [[Category:Flora of the Mediterranean basin]] [[Category:Plants described in 1753]] [[Category:Botanical taxa named by Carl Linnaeus]] [[Category:Flora of Malta]]
